title: Accessory Drive Locations — 3.7L Duratec
introduction:
I use this drawing to separate the engine’s external belt drives before trying to identify a pulley. Match each circled callout to the adjacent table, then trace the blue belt paths on the illustration. This reference applies to the 3.7L Duratec arrangement.

The crankshaft belt pulley supplies the rotation. The accessory belt carries that motion to the coolant pump and generator pulleys, while the spring-loaded tensioner keeps the accessory belt under tension. The coolant pump circulates coolant; the generator supplies electrical power and charges the battery. Think of the belt as a delivery route: the pulleys share the motion, but each destination has a different job.

The A/C compressor has a separately identified belt and pulley. I keep that path distinct from the accessory belt rather than assuming the tensioner controls both. Also distinguish a pulley from the assembly behind it: the compressor pulley is the belt-contact wheel, not the entire refrigerant compressor.

This map teaches component identity and the illustrated belt layout. It does not supply belt-release movements, removal instructions, tension specifications or fault tests. Once you have identified the relevant drive, use its matching service procedure before disturbing it; these external belts are separate from the engine’s internal timing chains.
